class.name: JRPGMessageText
class.brief_description: Control codes in message text: values from the game, colors, icons, sizes, waits and positions.
class.description: Text shown in messages, choices and database fields can hold control codes. [method expand] replaces those that stand for game data: [code]\V[n][/code] (the value of variable n), [code]\N[n][/code] (the name of actor n), [code]\P[n][/code] (the name of the n-th party member, 1 being the leader) and [code]\G[/code] (the currency unit). [code]\V[/code] comes first, so [code]\N[\V[3]][/code] names the actor whose id variable 3 holds. [method parse] turns the remaining codes into a list of operations for a message window: [code]\C[n][/code] text color, [code]\I[n][/code] icon, [code]\{[/code] and [code]\}[/code] one size step bigger or smaller, [code]\FS[n][/code] font size, [code]\$[/code] gold window, [code]\.[/code] and [code]\|[/code] waits of [constant SHORT_WAIT_FRAMES] and [constant LONG_WAIT_FRAMES] frames, [code]\![/code] wait for the player, [code]\>[/code] and [code]\<[/code] instant display on and off, [code]\^[/code] no wait for the player at the end (wherever it stands in the text), [code]\PX[n][/code] and [code]\PY[n][/code] text position, in pixels from the top left of the area inside the window's padding (the reference's help counts from the window's corner). [code]\\[/code] is a backslash. Codes are read without regard to case; a code that is not in this list, or whose [code][n][/code] is malformed, is shown as written. Online, servers send text keys and arguments and clients expand and show the text. Authority: client. Text is expanded and shown where it is read.

method.name: escape
method.description: Returns [param text] with every backslash doubled, so it shows as written in a message: a player's name, or text from outside the game.

method.name: expand
method.description: Returns [param text] with [code]\V[n][/code], [code]\N[n][/code], [code]\P[n][/code] and [code]\G[/code] replaced from [param state] and its database. A variable never set gives 0; an actor or a party slot that does not exist gives empty text. The values put in are text, never codes: their backslashes come out escaped (see [method escape]), so a name holding [code]\C[2][/code] shows it as written and a variable holding [code]\V[n][/code] is not expanded again. Without a game state the text is returned as it is.

method.name: parse
method.description: Returns the operations of [param text], in order, as dictionaries: [code]op[/code] (an [enum Op] value) and, depending on it, [code skip-lint]text[/code], [code]index[/code], [code]size[/code], [code]frames[/code], [code]x[/code] or [code]y[/code]. Consecutive text is one operation; each line break is an [constant OP_NEW_LINE].

method.name: strip
method.description: Returns the text of [param text] without its codes: [code]\\[/code] gives one backslash, icons are dropped and line breaks are kept.
